key_insight: SciExam for ENSO shows that language-model agents can build climate models that outperform a published benchmark even when the true answer is unknown.
engineering_relevance: This suggests AI agents could become practical tools for scientific model discovery and evaluation in computational science workflows where success must be measured by out-of-sample physical behavior, not by matching a fixed label.
method: Agents ingest real ENSO observations within a 6-hour budget.
They generate and freeze their own diagnostics, then iterate on a low-order stochastic model using only those diagnostics as feedback.
Hidden graders evaluate statistical fidelity, latent-variable reconstruction, and forecasting on held-out years, and compare against a published model.
evidence_signal: Across 12 agent systems, 6 produced models scoring above the published baseline, mainly due to better reconstruction and forecasting on hidden tests.
watch_item: The benchmark is promising, but results may still depend strongly on the specific information provided to each agent and on how well the hidden evaluation captures scientific validity.
paper_title: SciExam for ENSO: Can AI Agents Build Climate Models?
